entries.test: Public commissioning records and operating-capacity disclosures available at publication would show whether evidence supported more than a few hundred megawatts of Microsoft capacity coming online.
entries.note: This concerns the available evidence, not a firm ceiling on actual capacity.
The combined claim offers a probable explanation for Microsoft's silence. Its construction-status component can be checked separately.

entries.test: Public announcements, planning records and reporting available at publication would establish whether other identical Fairwater sites had been identified.
entries.note: He asserts an absence of identifying evidence, not that the other facilities definitively do not exist.
Deliberate obfuscation attributes a private intention. The separate question of publicly documented capacity is checkable.

entries.test: Public groundbreaking and operational-opening dates for comparable data centers would establish whether construction typically took around 18 months.
entries.note: The proposition preserves his approximate duration and qualified generalization.

entries.test: Construction updates, permits and commissioning records for the projects discussed would establish whether most remained unfinished years after groundbreaking.
entries.note: The scope is his surveyed projects, not every data center worldwide.

entries.test: Public project timelines, capacities and original completion schedules would establish typical construction durations and whether larger projects missed schedules more often.
entries.note: The size comparison describes an empirical relationship in completion rates.
The normalization adds a separate 'possibly' hedge to bill-and-hold. The source presents the account under an overall 'likely' qualification.
'Stinks of desperation' is a rhetorical characterization without a shared factual test.

entries.test: Microsoft revenue disclosures, customer-concentration reporting and paid Copilot subscriber figures would establish the size, composition and growth sources of its AI revenue run rate.
entries.note: Removing the insult about subscribers does not change the factual proposition.

entries.test: Public evidence on compute orders, utilization, shortages and newly commissioned capacity would establish whether supply constraints explain the apparent excess demand.
entries.note: In context, 'insatiable' refers to the claim of extraordinary demand inferred from compute shortages.
The numerical trigger is concrete, but the claim that only Huang and a construction firm receive value is rhetorical exaggeration.
The combined claim includes what every builder privately realized. Construction constraints and spending effects can be investigated separately.

entries.test: Public construction-progress and full-campus commissioning records would establish whether, at the stated pace, Abilene finished before mid-2027 or the remaining Oracle capacity before 2030.
entries.note: The forecast retains the 'at this rate' condition. Both specified time boundaries remain in the future.
'Likely' explicitly qualifies the predicted ordering of completion and financial exhaustion.

entries.test: Oracle's public financial disclosures and segment reporting would establish existing-business profitability, growth sources and GPU-compute margins relative to Microsoft and Google.
entries.note: This describes Oracle's current financial position under a potential delay scenario.

entries.test: Public evidence of Anthropic's subscription subsidies, available compute and capacity-related service restrictions would establish whether capacity constraints persist while subsidies continue.
entries.note: The future commitment uses 'will' and has no deadline; 'suggests' qualifies the present diagnosis.

entries.test: Public retrofit records and capacity commissioning disclosures from 2023 through publication would establish whether evidence showed each hyperscaler adding more than a few hundred megawatts.
entries.note: The capacity component concerns the evidence he found, rather than an unqualified ceiling on installed capacity.

entries.test: Public data-center completion records, NVIDIA shipment totals and installed-GPU or inventory reporting would establish whether unfinished deployment represented years of chip absorption.
entries.note: The conditional conclusion concerns chips already sold, so it is not a future forecast.
'Probably' explicitly qualifies the proposed condition of a selected data center.
Neither the relevant financial measure nor the degree of infrastructure mismatch is specified sufficiently for a shared test.
'It feels like' and 'might' frame this as a possibility rather than a firm assertion.
